KEY MESSAGE 1...

We have an Enhance Risk for Severe Thunderstorms for much of 
the area today into tonight, along with a Slight Risk for 
Excessive Rainfall and a Flood Watch for Flash Flooding.

Long wave trough in the east/ridge in the west pattern 
amplification takes place today via an embedded short-wave 
trough crossing the forecast and county warning area, a pattern
forecast to then persist for an extended period.

Contrary to the synoptic norm, the embedded short wave is ahead
of a strong cold front that will cross the area overnight
tonight into Wednesday morning. This less common setup has the 
major implication of heightened convective threats ahead of the
cold front, particularly as it is nearly coincident with daytime
heating, perhaps a tad early.

A high shear, moisture rich pre-storm environment will be in 
place, with 0-6 band 0-8 km shear of 40 to 60 kts, CAPE reaching
at least 2 KJ/kg, and as high as 4 KJ/kg in the Huntington Tri-
State area, along with PW values of 2 to as high as 2.5 inches,
again highest in the Huntington Tri-State area. This will 
encourage convective development in the middle Ohio Valley 
midday into this afternoon, and organization this afternoon that
crosses the central Appalachians this evening. Outflow 
boundaries from early morning convective complexes over the 
Midwest and over the Great Lakes may focus development into the
middle Ohio Valley midday and early this afternoon.

Discrete convection will carry a damaging wind threat as well 
as hail and a tornado threat, with the damaging wind threat 
becoming the more dominant threat as the convection organizes 
into lines or line segments. However, impressive low level flow 
for mid to late July, 40 to 50 kts at h85 and 30 to 40 kts at 
h925, contribute to 0-3 km shear of 30 to 40 kts this afternoon 
and evening, with the help of low LCLs, elevates the Significant
Tornado Parameter above 2 later this afternoon and evening, 
which could carry the Tornado threat longer. In addition, strong
flow through the column, veering in the low to mid levels and 
at times in the mid to upper levels, gives rise to curved 
hodographs throughout much of the Tuesday/Tuesday night period, 
with all three severe weather hazards, damaging wind, tornado 
and hail, at play to at least some degree this afternoon and
evening.

The round of convection midday through this afternoon will 
leave behind a cool pool suppressing surface based instability 
for a time this afternoon. Driven by a more subtle embedded 
short wave driving the surface cold front toward the area this 
evening, the strength of showers and thunderstorms ahead of the 
cold front itself this evening will depend upon how much the 
atmosphere can recover, but the high shear environment will 
encourage organization any convection that can get going into a 
line or line segments, which, together with h85 peaking in the 
40-50 kt range this evening, could give rise to a second 
damaging wind threat and even tornado and hail given the 
aforementioned wind profile factors, this evening.

The Storm Prediction Center has maintained the enhanced risk 
for severe thunderstorms for all but far southern portions of 
the forecast and county warning area, with all three severe 
weather hazards at play Tuesday into Tuesday night. Have 
included severe weather wording in the forecast for this 
afternoon into this evening.

In addition, the rich moisture, with surface dew points in the
mid 70s F, h85 theta e values up to around 350 K and PW values 
up to around two inches, contributes to significant instability
as will as high rainfall rates. With high convective coverage,
and wind profiles favoring training/backbuilding as suggested by
CAMs, flash flooding is likely to become an issue wherever 
heavy rainfall is most persistent or repetitive. HREF 6-0hour
Flash Flood Guidance probabilities exceed 50 percent for much 
of the area this afternoon, and, in coordination with 
neighboring offices, have issued a Flood Watch for Flash 
Flooding for nearly all of the area for this afternoon through 
tonight.

The Weather Prediction Center has a slight risk for excessive 
rainfall throughout the forecast and county warning area for 
Tuesday and Tuesday night.

Morning update forthcoming.
